description: PI-Detection is a Python and Jupyter workflow published by its repository contributors to identify electricity towers and poles from high-resolution satellite imagery. The repository documents image tiling, annotation conversion, training-set construction and detector training with Detectron2. Its worked inputs are WorldView-3 imagery from Vietnam; workflow notes describe 0.3 m processing and a remaining 0.4 m resampling task. GeoTIFF inputs are converted to PNG tiles, while polygon annotations are handled through GeoJSON and JSON. Source files, environment information and workflow documentation are available through GitHub under the MIT licence at no cost. The software licence does not grant access to the separately licensed satellite imagery. Documentation contains manual steps and the code was not installed or executed during this review. A modeller could use the workflow to prepare local power-asset inventories before hazard-exposure or digital-twin work. Its detections would still need engineering checks and network attributes. It complements existing power-system data records as an asset-extraction tool; it is not itself a power-flow simulator.
